Commentary.Commentary: So, 259 is the target for New Zealand. They have the batting line-up to chase this down but have shown signs of over-dependency on one-two players. Australia, on the other hand, need to bowl extremely well to defend this. Will the Kiwis chase this down or will Australia go 1-0 up? Join us in a short while to find out.

Australia started in an excellent fashion, courtesy David Warner and Aaron Finch. They both got to their respective fifties but then the problem started as they fell in quick succession and Australia could not recover from those blows. Steven Smith, too, could not last long and it was upon his disciple, Marnus Labuschagne who didn't disappoint and played a handy knock in helping the hosts reach 258. He got to his second fifty and it was a brilliant innings. The death overs was a problem as they could not find the boundaries at regular intervals. They scored only 64 runs in the last 10 overs and have ended up with a below-par score.

New Zealand have made a terrific comeback after Australia had got off to a brilliant start. The Aussies were 124/0 and were looking set for a total above 300 but the Kiwis pulled things back remarkably well and have restricted the Aussies to 258. Lockie Ferguson started it all, picking up the big wicket of David Warner and then Santner joined the party, getting Finch and the big fish, Steven Smith. He was the best bowler on show for the visitors, picking up two wickets and was the most economical as well. Sodhi was disappointing at the start but came back strongly in the end and finished with three wickets.

OUT! BOWLED! Not often you go through the defense of Steven Smith. Santner this time goes quicker through the air. He fires it in flat and a touch short around off at 92.6 kph, Smith spots the line and length early and finds it to be good enough to attempt for the back foot punch. But it skids off the surface and hurries past his bat to disturb the off pole. Smith cannot believe what has happened here! He looks at the pitch and then the stumps. Completely bamboozled. New Zealand enjoying a brilliant passage of play on the back of Santner's heroics!

Good length ball on off, Warner guides it to the third man region for a single.
Back of a length ball on off, Warner removes his one hand of the handle of the bat and defends it onto the pitch.

Uppish but safe! Back of a length ball on middle, Warner hops and then looks to flick but it takes the leading edge and goes to the left of the bowler. Boult moves to that side but the ball falls short.
Good length ball outside off, angling away. Warner looks to defend at first but then decides to leave it alone.
Full delivery outside off, Finch comes down the track and drives it to deep cover for a single.
Well fielded! Full toss on middle, Finch drives it towards mid on. Colin de Grandhomme comes across and then dives to make the stop.
BEATEN! Good way to finish the over! Good length ball outside off, Warner looks to defend but the ball whizzes past the bat and goes into the mitts of the keeper.
Very full delivery outside off, Warner lunges and then looks to drive but fails to get any bat on it.
Full delivery outside off, Warner pushes it to cover.
FOUR! Just wide of the mid-wicket fielder! Short ball on off, Warner pulls it uppishly but it is wide of the fielder and the ball races to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Full delivery on off, Finch drives it through point for a single.
FOUR! First boundary for Aaron Finch! Short of a length delivery, Finch pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
FOUR! Creamed! Full delivery outside off, Warner lunges forward and drives it through the cover region for a boundary. First one of the game.
Full on off, Warner pushes it to mid off.
Length ball on off, Warner defends it off the back foot.
Full on middle, Finch drives it to mid on and takes a single.

An appeal for caught behind turned down. Short ball around middle, Finch looks to pull but misses. Boult is confident that he has edged it and starts celebrating but the umpire is not interested. Taylor wants Williamson to take the review but in the end, Williamson decides against it. Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there was no bat on it. Good decision not to review.
Good length ball around off, nipping in. Finch looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a length on the pads, Warner attempts to tuck it to the leg side but misses. He gets hit on the pads but no harm done.
Good length ball outside off, Warner looks to defend but it takes the inside edge and hits Warner on the pads.
Ferguson is not getting his line right to Warner! Bowls another one on the pads, Warner whips it towards mid-wicket for a couple.
Fullish ball outside off, Finch drives it to covers and picks up a single.
LEG BYE! Length ball on the pads, Warner looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball goes to square leg and the batters cross for a leg bye.
Ferguson starts with a full delivery on the pads, Warner flicks it through mid-wicket and gets a couple before the fielder comes across and cleans it up.
Lockie Ferguson to bowl from the other end.
Finch is off the mark! Good length ball on middle and leg, Finch tucks it to the deep square leg region and picks up a couple. 3 from the first over.
Yorker on middle, Finch manages to dig it out back to the bowler. Good bowling from Trent Boult.
Full delivery on middle, Finch drives but Boult does well to field it.
Length ball outside off, Finch dances down the track and then pushes it back to the bowler.
Australia are underway! Good length ball on the pads, Warner looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls to square leg. The batters steal a leg bye.
Boult starts with a length ball outside off, angling away. Warner pushes it to the cover fielder.

We are all set to begin! The Kiwi players are in a huddle before making their way out to the middle. They are followed by David Warner and Aaron Finch. Trent Boult will start with the ball for the visitors.

Kane Williamson, the Kiwi skipper, says that they would have batted first as well. States that the series against India was a great one. Goes on to say that they are going with 2 seamers and 2 spinners.

Aaron Finch, the Australian skipper, says the wicket looks good to bat on. Adds that they weren't at their best in the South Africa series. States that it feels weird that there is no crowd at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Martin Guptill, Henry Nicholls, Kane Williamson (C), Ross Taylor, Tom Latham (WK), James Neesham, Colin de Grandhomme, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
Australia (Playing XI) - Aaron Finch (C), David Warner, Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, D'Arcy Short, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (wk), Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.
Toss - Australia have won the toss and they choose to bat first.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the first ODI between Australia and New Zealand. Despite the Coronavirus concerns affecting many sporting events in the world, these two teams are all set to lock horns in a 3-match ODI series. Australia had a tough series against South Africa and now would look for home comforts to get back to winning ways. They have retained the same squad that played the Proteas but Kane Richardson has been tested for COVID-19 and will miss this game. Sean Abbott has been called up to the squad as a standby. New Zealand, on the other hand, will be high on confidence after their victory against India and will be looking to continue the winning momentum. Trent Boult, Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry return to the squad, further bolstering their squad. Cricket Australia has announced that this series will be played behind closed doors due to Covid-19 virus. Will the Kiwis start the series with a win or will Australia get back to winning ways? Toss and team updates in a while.
